title: Journal Technologies court portal outage, Nov 13, 2026
disclaimer: Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by Journal Technologies, any court, news outlet, government agency, company, or anyone else named.
size_basis: The vendor serves courts in several states and countries. Court notices and press show portals offline at many courts in California, Illinois, Nevada and Washington; the Sacramento Bee counts 20 California superior courts. The vendor gives no total, so size rests on reported reach.
who_is_affected: People and lawyers who use online case lookup, e-filing or reservation systems at courts that use the vendor's portal software. Courts say to file in person and to call clerk's offices meanwhile. Courts' own case-management systems are said to be separate from the portals.

known.text: Journal Technologies says suspicious, malicious automated activity targeted its public portal software, first identified on Nov 13.
The vendor advised customers to take their public portals offline, and courts did.
Public portals or e-filing were offline at many courts, including Alameda, Kern, Marin, Ventura, Riverside, Los Angeles, Spokane, Lake County, Illinois, and King County, Washington.
Kern's court says its portal is offline and gives no estimated restoration time.

not_known.text: Whether any data was exposed; the vendor says it has found no evidence so far for Criminal Justice Information and is still investigating.
When every affected portal will be restored, and how many courts are affected.
Whether this is connected to the other outages reported this week.
